counting_methodology_frozen_before_count.basis: all-fragments (Rust-only shard; this worker did not have access to the other nine languages' fragments needed to compute the common basis intersection). This must be flagged by the runner: per interaction_with_quality_metrics.common_basis_rule, primary A-D/E figures should be computed on the common basis across all ten languages once all fragments exist; this shard supplies Rust's all-fragments raw material only.
counting_methodology_frozen_before_count.capability_points_denominator_note: supported_capability_points = sum over the 44 probes of capability_points(=2) * support_factor(Rust). Rust was assessed FULL (support_factor=1) on every one of the 44 probes based on documented standard-library/language mechanisms (see support_determinations below), giving 44*2*1 = 88.
categories: SF = distinct syntax forms required to express/interpret the probe's supported fragment (counting rule: one count per distinct token-level construct not already counted for this probe, e.g. a keyword, operator, macro invocation, attribute, or standard-library call form)

CD = context-dependent rules (a rule whose meaning depends on where/how the construct is used, e.g. borrow-checker admissibility, trait-bound resolution, move-vs-borrow inferred from callee signature)
IM = implicit rules (behavior triggered without local written syntax, e.g. default integer type inference, implicit Drop call at scope end, deref coercion, closure capture-mode inference)

EX = documented semantic exceptions (a specific documented deviation from the 'normal' rule for this construct, e.g. panic-on-out-of-range, checked-vs-release overflow behavior, HashMap iteration order left unspecified)
counting_methodology_frozen_before_count.unknown_vs_zero_rule: Per spec 6.1.4.E and section 20, a sub-count is recorded 'unknown' rather than 0 only when no specification text exists to count against. For every probe below, Rust's language reference / std documentation exists and was consultable in principle for all four categories, so 0 was only ever recorded as an actual observed absence of that category for that specific probe (e.g. F08.P2 has no additional documented exception beyond the checked-division API itself), never as a stand-in for missing documentation.

limitations_and_caveats: This is a single-worker, packet-only, no-toolchain-execution estimate. Per V1 (pre_measurement_validation), every fragment scored FULL or PARTIAL must actually build/run under the frozen recipe; this worker had no compiler access and could not execute rustc. The support determinations and complexity counts above are reasoned from documented, well-established Rust language/std-library semantics but are NOT yet backed by an executed build/run evidence record (build command, exit status, observed stdout) as V1 requires. This is recorded as an infrastructure limitation of this packet-only worker, not a finding that Rust lacks the capability.

The complexity-unit itemization (SF/CD/IM/EX) is this worker's frozen-before-counting categorical breakdown applied consistently probe-by-probe; it is auditable via the per_probe_complexity_units table and the mechanisms table, but was not cross-checked against an independently authored R10 alternative-form record with token counts and documentation citations, which the full methodology also requires for each probe.

Only Rust was assigned to this shard; no comparative data for the other nine languages is available here. The placeholder_normalized_score (100/(1+E)) is NOT the spec's true cross-language-normalized Capability Efficiency score and must be replaced by the runner once all ten languages' raw E values are merged.
evidence.normalization_note: This packet is a single-language shard (per primary.json max_requirement_ids_per_multi_language_agent / language-sharded assignment). Per spec 6.1.4.E, Capability Efficiency = counted semantic-complexity units / supported capability points, counted on the same basis as metrics A-D. The frozen methodology does not specify a self-contained 0-100 normalization for a single language in isolation; final normalization (spec 6.1.7, 27.1 table 'higher = better') requires min-max or comparable scaling across all ten languages' raw E values, which is runner-only aggregation (primary.json runner.aggregation = 'runner_only'). This worker reports (a) the raw, fully-itemized E value for Rust and (b) a documented monotonic placeholder transform so the schema's 0-100 slot is populated pending merge: normalized_placeholder = 100 / (1 + E). The runner must replace this placeholder with the true cross-language-normalized score once all language shards for metric.capability_efficiency are merged; this value must not be hand-copied into the final ranking (rule 11 of worker_core.md).
